definitions.explanation: Vinegar made from grains such as wheat, corn, or rice. A common, mild-flavored vinegar used in everyday Japanese cooking.

examples.japanese: {穀物酢|こくもつす}で{酢|す}の{物|もの}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made a vinegared dish with grain vinegar.

examples.japanese: {穀物酢|こくもつす}は{値段|ねだん}が{手頃|てごろ}で{使|つか}いやすい。
examples.english: Grain vinegar is affordable and easy to use.

examples.japanese: {米酢|こめず}に{比|くら}べて{穀物酢|こくもつす}は{味|あじ}がさっぱりしていて、どんな{料理|りょうり}にも{合|あ}う。
examples.english: Compared to rice vinegar, grain vinegar has a lighter taste and goes with any dish.

notes:
A compound of {穀物|こくもつ} (grain/cereal) and {酢|す} (vinegar). This is the most common and affordable type of vinegar in Japanese kitchens. It is made from a blend of grains (typically wheat, corn, and rice) and has a milder, more neutral flavor than pure {米酢|こめず} (rice vinegar).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {穀物酢|こくもつす}で{味付|あじつ}けする: to season with grain vinegar
- {穀物酢|こくもつす}を{薄|うす}める: to dilute grain vinegar
- {純|じゅん}{穀物酢|こくもつす}: pure grain vinegar

TYPES OF VINEGAR:
- {米酢|こめず}: rice vinegar (richer flavor, made from rice only)
- {黒酢|くろず}: black vinegar (aged, full-bodied flavor)
- {果実酢|かじつす}: fruit vinegar (apple, grape, etc.)
- {寿司酢|すしず}: seasoned sushi vinegar (pre-mixed with sugar and salt)
